subject.title: [Security] Unsafe Default Permissions on Downloaded Plugin Temp Files in clawhub-install-records.ts

question: Does the current ClawHub download path permit a second OS user to traverse the cache directory and read the artifact, or is it already isolated by the managed per-user temp root?
rationale: The answer determines whether this is a real confidentiality boundary bypass, defense-in-depth hardening, or a trust-model mismatch; the issue body does not provide enough effective-permission evidence to decide safely.

options.title: Request private reproduction
options.body: Ask for a current-main multi-user reproduction with directory and file modes, then harden the standard temp-helper path if cross-user access succeeds.

options.title: Treat as hardening
options.body: Add explicit owner-only directory and file modes with focused POSIX tests even if the existing parent directory already blocks traversal.

options.title: Close after verification
options.body: Close as non-reproducible only if current-main testing proves the artifact is inaccessible to another OS user through every supported temp path.

recommendation.title: Request private reproduction
recommendation.body: Ask for a current-main multi-user reproduction with directory and file modes, then harden the standard temp-helper path if cross-user access succeeds.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to recent plugin-install hardening and review decisions around the affected control-plane surface.
